body.input: Which AI companies entered the Danish market in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, there is no single comprehensive list of AI companies that entered the Danish market specifically in 2026. However, here is what can be gathered about notable AI-related market developments in Denmark during 2026:

## Key AI Market Developments in Denmark (2026)

### Domestic AI Ecosystem Growth
- Denmark's AI sector has been mapped in the first **AI Report Denmark** (published September 2026), identifying **1,249 AI tools and companies** headquartered in Denmark (based on June 2026 data). The report was compiled by RankmyAI in cooperation with Aalborg University Business School and AI Denmark.
- AI adoption among Danish companies surged — **59% of companies** with more than 10 employees now use AI (up from 15% in 2023), making Denmark the European leader in workplace AI implementation.

### Major AI Infrastructure Investment
- **Netcompany** invested DKK 325 million (~€43.6 million) in the **Danish Centre for AI Innovation (DCAI)** in November 2026, acquiring a 23.7% stake. DCAI operates the **Gefion AI supercomputer**, Denmark's sovereign AI platform.
- **EIFO** (Denmark's Export and Investment Fund) added DKK 150 million, bringing the total new investment to approximately DKK 500 million (~€67 million).
- **TDC Erhverv** launched a go-to-market collaboration with DCAI to bring AI supercomputing access to Danish businesses and public institutions.

### New AI-Focused Entrants
- **Lumeo**, an AI visibility agency for B2B companies, was founded in Denmark in 2026.
- **Velatir** has been active in the Danish market, with representatives speaking at AI implementation events (e.g., FÆLLES AI Implementering in Nyborg Strand).

### Data Center Expansion Supporting AI
- **Caverion Denmark** and **Assemblin Sweden** entered into an agreement to deliver technical installations for the expansion of a data center in Denmark, reflecting growing AI infrastructure demand.

Denmark's 2026 government platform explicitly set the ambition for the country to become a frontrunner in developing and responsibly applying AI, which has been a key driver of these developments. However, a definitive list of international AI companies that specifically "entered" the Danish market in 2026 is not available from current sources.

Lumeo was founded in Denmark in 2026 as an AI visibility agency for B2B companies, representing a new AI‑focused entrant to the Danish market.
Velatir has been active in the Danish market in 2026, with representatives speaking at AI implementation events, indicating its presence as an AI company operating in Denmark.

No comprehensive list of international AI companies entering Denmark in 2026 is available, as the sources focus on domestic growth and infrastructure investments rather than specific foreign market entries.

10 November 2026

Netcompany invests in Danish Centre for AI Innovation A/S, the company behind the Gefion AI supercomputer

Netcompany Group A/S (“Netcompany”) has today agreed to invest in Danish Centre for AI Innovation A/S (“DCAI”), the company running the Danish AI supercomputer ‘Gefion’, alongside the existing shareholders Novo Nordisk Fonden (“NNF”) and Danmarks Eksport- og Investeringsfond (“EIFO”).

The transaction  
The transaction is a primary investment, with Netcompany, NNF and EIFO investing approximately DKK 500 million in aggregate, at the same price per share and on identical terms. Netcompany has subscribed for new shares in DCAI for DKK 325 million, based on a pre-money valuation of DKK 875 million. [...] “Denmark will undoubtedly increase the use of responsible and sovereign AI – the question is whether the value is created here in Denmark or somewhere else. Gefion gives Denmark a unique starting point. Together with Novo Nordisk Fonden and EIFO, we will transform DCAI’s GPU compute foundation into a scalable, secure and commercially viable national AI platform supporting the Danish public sector, critical Danish industries, and research and educational institutions. We are doing this securely and at scale based on DCAI’s original ambitions in AI and on high-performance computing – and in a sovereign setting on Danish soil. We see tremendous value for Denmark and other similar countries with same ambitions, DCAI, and Netcompany in this transaction. Denmark will effectively be the first [...] Strategic rationale  
DCAI and the Danish AI supercomputer ‘Gefion’ form a significant part of Denmark’s AI capacity. Together with NNF and EIFO, Netcompany will work to further develop this foundation from a GPU asset into a scalable, secure, and commercially viable national AI platform that can support the Danish public sector, critical Danish industries, and research and educational institutions. The Danish AI supercomputer ‘Gefion’ is already serving users in defence, research, healthcare, etc., while demand for secure and sovereign AI capacity in Denmark and Europe is growing rapidly.

# AI Visibility Agency in Denmark for B2B Companies

By Carl Baggesen, founder of Lumeo · Last updated 12 November 2026

Lumeo is an AI visibility agency in Denmark for B2B startups and scaleups. We work to get your company and your CEO named when buyers ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI who to hire. Every month we write LinkedIn posts, website pages and placement pitches, and we run one data experiment. We track 50 of your buyers' questions every day in four AI apps, so you can see what changed.

Lumeo is an agency, not software. It was founded in 2026 and is based in Denmark. We work month to month, and you can start with a free Snapshot.

## Why does AI visibility matter for a B2B company? [...] ## Who is Lumeo for, and who is it not for?

Lumeo works with B2B startups and scaleups based in Denmark whose buyers research suppliers with ChatGPT and Google.

An agency does the work, and software measures whether it happens. The Danish overview at aivisibility.dk splits providers into these two kinds: agencies that work to get brands mentioned in AI answers, and platforms that measure whether it happens.

context.content:
The investment also supports Denmark’s ambition, as set out in the 2026 government platform, to become a frontrunner in developing and responsibly applying AI. The government intends to provide €20 million (DKK 150 million) to increase public commitment through EIFO.

Gefion already serves users in defence, research, academia, healthcare and industry, but market analysis points to an addressable market many times DCAI's current scale, highlighting the opportunity for further capacity expansion.

Martin Svensson, CEO of DCAI, says: [...] Martin Svensson, CEO of DCAI, says:

> “When Gefion was inaugurated in 2024, the main task was to train large AI models. Today, companies and public organisations are building AI into their products and workflows, and a new generation of AI agents is taking on more complex tasks. DCAI will now be able to build modern AI capacity that public institutions and businesses can trust and adopt, not least where data is sensitive or regulated.”

“The real value of Gefion will not be measured in computing power alone. It will be measured by what Denmark and Europe are able to build with it,” says André Rogaczewski, CEO of Netcompany. [...] With the supercomputer Gefion, Denmark has already established a world-class foundation for AI. Now, the ambition is to take the next step: extending access to that capability across a much broader part of Danish society and helping organisations move from AI experimentation to real-world adoption.

The partners aim to strengthen a shared, sovereign national AI platform that reduces barriers to advanced AI adoption, particularly for public institutions, regulated industries and smaller businesses.

The partnership brings together DCAI’s advanced AI infrastructure with Netcompany’s experience in developing and operating some of Europe’s most complex and society-critical digital systems.
